# Checkpoints at a Glance, and Answers {#sec-checkpoints}

```{python}
#| label: appE-setup
# The water rebuild's model answer, computed: run the finished analysis again with
# MAX_MISSING = 1 instead of its setting, in memory, and compare, following Tunja and the
# department capitals' rural zones through the change.
from scripts import water as w
from scripts.prose import number_words, text_holds

# The water exercises' opening puzzle (chapters/exercises-water.qmd), answered by the function that
# planted it, so the answer cannot drift from the puzzle.
honest_w, planted_w = w.council_claims(w.res())

NUM = number_words(zero="no")
A = w.A
full = w.res()
before = full["summary"]
original = A.MAX_MISSING
A.MAX_MISSING = 1
try:
    stricter = A.run()
finally:
    A.MAX_MISSING = original
after = stricter["summary"]
c0, c1 = full["clusters"], stricter["clusters"]
keys = ["divipola", "zone", "year"]
gone = c0.merge(c1[keys], on=keys, how="left", indicator=True)
gone = gone[gone["_merge"] == "left_only"]             # the rows the stricter rule drops
capital = gone["department_capital"] == 1
n_cap_rural = int((capital & (gone["zone"] == "rural")).sum())
n_cap_urban = int((capital & (gone["zone"] == "urban")).sum())
n_other = len(gone) - n_cap_rural
cap_rural0 = c0[(c0["department_capital"] == 1) & (c0["zone"] == "rural")]
tj0, tj1 = c0[c0["divipola"] == "15001"], c1[c1["divipola"] == "15001"]
tj_rural0 = int((tj0["zone"] == "rural").sum())
tj_c = int(tj0["cluster"].iloc[0])
kept = c0.merge(c1, on=keys, suffixes=("_0", "_1"))
same = (kept["cluster_0"] == kept["cluster_1"]).mean()
# The rows reach the rule before imputation, so the flags show which values they were missing.
text_holds(original == 2 and gone[["water_coverage_imputed", "sewer_coverage_imputed"]].eq(1).all().all()
           and n_cap_rural == len(cap_rural0) > 0 and len(gone) == len(c0) - len(c1)
           and len(gone) == after["dropped_too_many_missing"] - before["dropped_too_many_missing"]
           and set(tj1["zone"]) == {"urban"} and tj1["cluster"].eq(tj_c).all()
           and len(tj1) == (tj0["zone"] == "urban").sum() and tj0["cluster"].eq(tj_c).all()
           and after["k"] == before["k"] == 4                 # the post's `assert k == 4`
           and list(stricter["profiles"]["name"]) == list(full["profiles"]["name"]),
           "the MAX_MISSING rebuild")
```

This appendix lists every checkpoint, then answers the book's exercises and planted errors, in
book order: the fast path's ROC AUC, a London input changed, the London table's wrong cell, the
pull request's recall, a water setting changed, and the sentence that claims a cause.

## Every checkpoint {.unnumbered}

Each checkpoint is a folder in `quarto-workshop/checkpoints/` holding a project as it stands at the end of
one hands-on block, with a README listing the steps to catch up: back up your folder (all but `.venv/`) to a
new time-stamped folder beside it, copy the checkpoint in (and, for the water project, `data/` if it is
missing), render and check a named output. Paste `Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/<path>/README.md`
into your agent, or follow the README by hand, then carry on from the section whose catch-up box you
used. The README names the workshop slide at the same point. There is no checkpoint 03.

Reading on your own, diagnose before you catch up. Check where you are (`pwd`), what changed since your last
commit (`git status`, then `git diff`) and the error's first line ([Reading an error](b-terminal.qmd#sec-keys-errors), @sec-troubleshooting), and
try the one fix it points to. Catch up only if that fails. Afterwards, open the output the README names and see
that it shows what the book describes at the catch-up box.

@sec-first-report has no checkpoint either. Its project is small and typed by hand, and its starter,
`starters/first-report/` in the same repository, is its fresh start: to begin again, rename your copy with
`mv ~/first-report ~/first-report-old` and copy the starter again as in @sec-first-files. Within the chapter,
your last commit is the known-good state: `git restore` takes a file back to it.

## Answer: the fast path's ROC AUC {.unnumbered #sec-answer-fast}

```{python}
#| label: appE-fast
# Chapter 3's opening sentence, from the function that planted it (scripts/evaluation.py).
from scripts import evaluation as ev

FAST = ev.fast_plant()
best_ev = ev.summary()["best_version"]
```

The sentence that opens @sec-fast-path reads "`{python} FAST["sentence"]`" The ROC AUC in it,
`{python} FAST["wrong"]`, is `{python} FAST["rival"]`'s; `{python} best_ev`'s is
`{python} FAST["right"]`, as `outputs/metrics.csv` shows. The name is right and the number was
copied from another row, a slip that inline code, which reads the file, cannot make.

## Answer: changing a London input {.unnumbered #sec-answer-london}

```{python}
#| label: appE-london
# The white paper copies ALVA's UK rank from the file: the Tower's rank there.
import pandas as pd

ldn_att = pd.read_csv("../examples/london/data/attractions.csv")
tower_rank_uk = int(ldn_att.loc[ldn_att["attraction"] == "Tower of London", "rank_uk"].iloc[0])
ORDINALS = ["zeroth", "first", "second", "third", "fourth", "fifth", "sixth", "seventh",
            "eighth", "ninth", "tenth"]
# The answer says the copied rank goes stale: the Tower is not first in the UK, and 8,000,000 visits
# would be the most of the ten.
text_holds(tower_rank_uk != 1
           and ldn_att.loc[ldn_att["attraction"] != "Tower of London", "visits_2025"].max() < 8_000_000,
           "the white paper's stale rank for the Tower")
```

The task (@sec-london-change): set the Tower of London's `visits_2025` to 8,000,000.

**What changes.** Every page that loads `attractions.csv` (@tbl-london-deps) is rebuilt with the new count,
and what it shows depends on its code. The guide, in every format it writes (web page, Word and PDF, and
PowerPoint, slides and EPUB if made), the dashboard's value boxes and bar chart, and the partner brief
(`london-email.docx`) find the top attraction with `idxmax()` and the total with `.sum()`, so the Tower of
London becomes the most visited attraction and the total rises. The square advert, if made, uses only
`idxmax()`, so it names the Tower too. The white paper names no top attraction: its sums by admission change,
but its table keeps ALVA's `rank_uk` column from the file, so it would still rank the Tower
`{python} ORDINALS[tower_rank_uk]` in the UK beside the most visits of the ten. A copied column goes stale too.

**What does not.** The flyer, which copies its facts and quotes no visit counts; the covering email
(`london-email-message.md`), which quotes no numbers and is not rendered; the dashboard's line chart and the
3-D map, which read `visits.csv`, not `attractions.csv`; any output not rebuilt; and the live site, until it is
published again.

**Why.** Every render re-runs every page's code (`freeze: false`), and each changed output is linked to the
input by a line of code that loads it. A strong answer names that line.

**Follow-up questions worth asking.** Where would the change appear if the number had been typed into the
prose instead of computed? (Nowhere: the typed number would silently disagree with the chart.) What would
change if `visits.csv` were edited instead? (The dashboard's line chart, the 3-D map and the white paper's
trend.) Why does the render re-run every cell? (Because nothing is cached; see @sec-water-website.)

## Answer: the London table's wrong cell {.unnumbered #sec-answer-london-value}

The puzzle at the start of [Part II's exercises](../chapters/exercises-london.qmd), found by
reading each of the five rows against `data/visits.csv`:

```{python}
#| label: appE-london-value
#| output: asis
# Part II's planted value (exercises-london.qmd, cell ex2-planted), from the same function the
# exercises print it with, so the puzzle and its answer cannot drift.
from scripts import london
ldn = london.planted_visits()
ldn_year, ldn_sight, ldn_printed, ldn_true = ldn["year"], ldn["sight"], ldn["printed"], ldn["true"]
ldn_more = "more" if ldn_printed > ldn_true else "fewer"
print(f"The wrong cell is in the row for {ldn_sight}. The table prints {ldn_printed:,}; its row in "
      f"`data/visits.csv` for {ldn_year} says {ldn_true:,}, so the table shows "
      f"{abs(ldn_printed - ldn_true):,} visits {ldn_more} than ALVA counted. The figure is not a "
      f"typo: it is that sight's {ldn_year - 1} count, a year out of date, in the right column and "
      f"the right units.")
```

## Answer: the pull request's recall {.unnumbered #sec-answer-team}

```{python}
#| label: appE-team
# Chapter 15's planted recall (team.qmd, cell team-plant), from the same ev.team_plant() the
# chapter prints it with. The gap is between the two figures as printed, in percentage points.
TP = ev.team_plant()
rival_ev, rec_best, rec_rival = TP["rival"], TP["right"], TP["value"]
rec_gap = f"{100 * abs(float(rec_best) - float(rec_rival)):.1f}"
rec_word = "higher" if float(rec_best) > float(rec_rival) else "lower"
```

The pull request of @sec-team-rules gives `{python} best_ev` a recall of `{python} rec_rival`:
that is `{python} rival_ev`'s, the same slip as [the fast path's](e-checkpoints.qmd#sec-answer-fast).
`{python} best_ev`'s own, in
`outputs/metrics.csv`, is `{python} rec_best`, `{python} rec_gap` percentage points
`{python} rec_word`. Of the three checks (@sec-three-checks), correctness found it: one number
traced to its row. Scope should have raised it first: a change described as "wording only"
changed a figure.

## Answer: changing a water setting {.unnumbered #sec-answer-water}

The task (@sec-water-change): set `MAX_MISSING = 1` instead of 2 in `scripts/analysis.py`. Computed here by
running the finished analysis both ways:

| | `MAX_MISSING = 2` | `MAX_MISSING = 1` |
|---|--:|--:|
| rows dropped for missing features | `{python} w.fmt(before["dropped_too_many_missing"])` | `{python} w.fmt(after["dropped_too_many_missing"])` |
| rows kept | `{python} w.fmt(before["kept"])` | `{python} w.fmt(after["kept"])` |
| municipalities | `{python} w.fmt(before["municipalities"])` | `{python} w.fmt(after["municipalities"])` |
| k | `{python} before["k"]` | `{python} after["k"]` |

: The water analysis with each setting. {#tbl-answer-water}

**The prediction.** Every row missing more than one of the `{python} NUM[len(A.FEATURES)]` features
goes. Department capitals have no
zone-level coverage, so their rural zones reach that rule with both coverage values missing (imputation comes
after the rule): every one of their rural zone-years goes, Tunja's `{python} NUM[tj_rural0]` among them,
while Tunja's urban zone, which takes the municipal total, stays.

**What the rebuild shows.** The stricter setting drops `{python} w.fmt(len(gone))` more rows, every one of them
missing both coverage values: the capitals' `{python} w.fmt(n_cap_rural)` rural zone-years and
`{python} w.fmt(n_other)` other zone-years whose coverage split is missing that year,
`{python} NUM[n_cap_urban]` of them capitals' urban zones with no municipal total either. Nothing else goes.
Tunja's urban zone stays in cluster `{python} tj_c` in every year. k stays `{python} after["k"]`, so the blog
post's `assert k == 4` still passes (a setting that changed k would make the post fail its render, by design),
the names stay, and `{python} f"{same:.0%}"` of the remaining rows keep their cluster.

**What changes.** `pre-render` re-runs `scripts/analysis.py`, which rewrites every file in `outputs/`
(`clusters.parquet`, `cluster_profiles.csv`, `k_selection.csv`, `stability.csv`, `outcomes_by_year.csv`,
`irca_infant.csv`, `irca_infant_bins.csv` and `summary.json`), and `freeze: false` re-executes every page, so
every page that reads `outputs/` changes (@tbl-water-deps): the clusters page, the report in every format,
the slides, the blog post, the dashboard and the white paper, which also quotes the setting itself.

**What does not.** `data/`, the page sources, the post's title (k is still `{python} after["k"]`) and, until it
is published again, the live site. Nor does the explore page: it re-runs, but reads only
`data/water_municipal.csv`.

**Why.** Compute once, publish many: one setting in one script, read by every publication. Strong answers name
the mechanism (`pre-render`, `outputs/`, `freeze: false`) and check at least two outputs against the new row
counts. Undo with `git restore scripts/analysis.py`.

## Answer: the sentence that claims a cause {.unnumbered #sec-answer-water-claims}

The puzzle at the start of [the water analysis's exercises](../chapters/exercises-water.qmd): sentence `{python} w.CLAIM_PLANTED + 1`. Its comparison is
true, read from `cluster_profiles.csv`, but its last words, "`{python} w.CLAIM_CAUSE`", claim a cause that no
comparison between kinds can show (@sec-causation). Written with verbs of association, it reads:

> `{python} honest_w[w.CLAIM_PLANTED]`
